chapter.v:
A message
about Tyre. Howl, people on the ships of Tarshish! Tyre has been destroyed—nothing is left of the houses and the harbor. They heard the news from the people of Cyprus.

Stay shocked
into silence, people of the coastlands, merchants of Sidon, and sailors.

Egyptian grain
came across the wide oceans. The Nile's harvest was what made Tyre money; she was the merchant to the nations.

Feel the
shame, Sidon! For the fortress of the sea says, “I have no children, having never been in labor or given birth. I have not brought up young men or brought up young women.”

When the
news about Tyre reaches Egypt they will be in agony.

Sail across
to Tarshish! Howl, people of the coastlands!

Is this
really your triumphant city, whose beginnings are from the distant past, who has sent out people to colonize faraway places?

Who planned
this attack on Tyre? Tyre, who created kingdoms, whose merchants were princes, whose traders were honored around the world!

The Lord
Almighty planned it, to humble its pride in all its glory, and to bring down all who receive worldly honor.

Work your
land, people of Tarshish, as they do beside the Nile, for you don't have a harbor anymore.

The Lord
held his hand out over the sea and shook kingdoms. He has condemned Phoenicia, giving the order to destroy their fortresses.

He said,
“Don't celebrate any more, mistreated virgin daughter of Sidon. Go and sail over to Cyprus—however, even there you won't find rest.”

Look at
the country of the Babylonians, this people that are not as they used to be! The Assyrians have turned it into a place for desert animals. They set up their siege towers, they demolished the fortresses, and ruined the country.

Howl, people
on the ships of Tarshish because your fortress is destroyed!

At that
time Tyre will be forgotten for seventy years, a king's lifetime, as it were. But at the end of these seventy years, Tyre will be like the song about a prostitute,

“Take a
lyre and walk around the city, forgotten prostitute! Play and sing so people will remember you!”

After seventy
years, the Lord will restore Tyre. But then she will go back to hiring herself out as a prostitute, selling herself to all the kingdoms of the world.

However, her
profits and what she earns will be consecrated to the Lord. They won't be kept or saved up, for her business earnings will go to those who worship the Lord, to provide them with plenty of food and good clothes.
